questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was about experiencing living in an English-speaking country and encountering new academic challenges.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: You also had to be proactive, but the UofT inbound office was good at disseminating information and responding to inquiries quite fast

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't really receive any assistance when I arrived, expect for an information meeting

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It wasn't that easy to find an affordable place. I got together with some of the other UCPH students and looked for an apartment together. We found an AirBnb we could rent privately.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend finding a place in walking distance to the university or nearby a TTC station.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of options but many of them were long-term rents or for at least a year.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First, you could see all the possible courses in their catalouge and create a possible schedule for your courses to make sure there wasn't any conflicts with the courses. Then they send out a formula for you to fill out with the relevant course requests.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They sent out guides on how to apply

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use some time to make a schedule for your courses and apply for them all in the first round. There's plenty of options to change and drop courses later on - so if I was in-between two courses I would apply for both of them and have the option to drop one of them later on.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I primarily had 3rd year courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Most of the courses I had were only lectures whereas I at UCPH also have instruction classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECO365H1 - International Monetary Economics
ECO316H1 - Applied Game Theory
ECO342H1 - Twentieth Century Economic History: Institutions, Growth and inequality
CSC108H1 - Introduction to Computer Programming

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend ECO316 and ECO342 if they're studying economics, because it can be transferred as Micro III and Economic History. 
And CSC108 was a great introduction course to Python.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not unexpected costs, but I would make room in my budget for experiences and travels.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I was surprised, that I didn't have to buy any books for my courses. There were some recommended books, but not any required ones.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of options, but I didn't really look that much into them

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sorts!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't really join any clubs. But I would recommend following all the different Instagram profiles, to see which activities there's going on.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would explore the city, go to hockey games or travel around (I would recommend paying Banff National Park a visit).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy actually. There's a lot of international students as well.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: To be honest, there were mostly international students in my classes, so I found it hard to socialize with local students. I mostly hung out with the other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The only thing that comes to my mind is the tax and tipping system - it's very different from Denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I think it's hard to say as Toronto is very multicultural. But generally the friendliness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend finding other exchange students as well.
Use the facilities at school - there are many great places to study, work out and such.
Don't be afraid to reach out to the offices, they're very helpsome and answers quite fast.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is a university in the middle of the city - so you don't get the same 'college'/campus experience as you might get other places in Canada.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The ability to live in another country and get to know a lot of other exchange students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My greatest challenge was to attend courses all alone and navigate through that.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
